title: Joshua Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 10.

questions.question: Who was the king of Jerusalem that heard about Joshua taking Ai?
questions.correctAnswer: Adonizedek
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:1 states that Adonizedek king of Jerusalem heard about Joshua taking Ai.

questions.question: Why did the kings fear greatly according to Joshua 10?
options: Because Gibeon was a great city and greater than Ai
questions.correctAnswer: Because Gibeon was a great city and greater than Ai
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:2 explains they feared greatly because Gibeon was a great city, greater than Ai, and its men were mighty.

questions.question: Which kings did Adonizedek send to help him fight against Gibeon?
questions.correctAnswer: Hoham, Piram, Japhia, Debir
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:3 names Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon as those Adonizedek sent.

questions.question: What was the reason Adonizedek gave for attacking Gibeon?
options: Because Gibeon made peace with Joshua and Israel
Because Gibeon refused to pay tribute
questions.correctAnswer: Because Gibeon made peace with Joshua and Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:4 states Adonizedek wanted to smite Gibeon because it had made peace with Joshua and the children of Israel.

questions.question: How many kings gathered together to make war against Gibeon?
questions.correctAnswer: Five
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:5 specifies that five kings of the Amorites gathered to fight Gibeon.

questions.question: From which place did the men of Gibeon send for Joshua's help?
questions.correctAnswer: Gilgal
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:6 says the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal for help.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua delayed before coming to help the men of Gibeon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:7 indicates Joshua ascended from Gilgal quickly with all the people of war.

questions.question: What did the LORD say to Joshua regarding the enemy?
options: Fear them not; I have delivered them into thine hand
questions.correctAnswer: Fear them not; I have delivered them into thine hand
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:8 records the LORD's words encouraging Joshua not to fear because the enemy was delivered into his hand.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua traveled all night from Gilgal to surprise the enemy.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:9 says Joshua came suddenly and went up from Gilgal all night.

questions.question: What did the LORD do to the enemy at Gibeon?
options: Discomfited them and slew them with great slaughter
Made them flee without a fight
questions.correctAnswer: Discomfited them and slew them with great slaughter
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:10 describes the LORD discomfiting the enemy and slaying them with a great slaughter at Gibeon.

questions.question: According to Joshua 10, how did more enemies die during the battle?
options: From hailstones cast down by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: From hailstones cast down by the LORD
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:11 states more died from hailstones cast down than by the sword of Israel.

questions.question: Who did Joshua ask to stand still in the day of battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Sun and Moon
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:12 shows Joshua asked the sun to stand still upon Gibeon and the moon in the valley of Ajalon.

questions.question: True or False: The sun and moon stood still for about a whole day as the Israelites avenged themselves.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:13 records the sun stood still and the moon stayed until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies.

questions.question: What did Joshua do after the LORD fought for Israel and the battle ended?
options: Returned to the camp at Gilgal with all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Returned to the camp at Gilgal with all Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:15 says Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal after the battle.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Gibeon made peace with Israel before the battle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:1 states the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Where did the five kings hide after fleeing from Joshua and Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: In a cave at Makkedah
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:16 states explicitly that the five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah, which is confirmed again in verse 17.

questions.question: What did Joshua command after hearing the five kings were found in the cave?
options: Roll great stones upon the cave's mouth and set men to guard it
Attack the cave immediately and kill the kings
Negotiate a peace treaty with the kings
Leave the kings to escape and pursue other enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Roll great stones upon the cave's mouth and set men to guard it
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:18 records Joshua's instruction to roll large stones over the cave entrance and place guards there, preventing the kings' escape while the army pursued other enemies.

questions.question: What did Joshua tell his army to do while the five kings were guarded in the cave?
options: Pursue their enemies and do not stop until they are defeated
Rest and prepare for a siege
Return to camp and wait for further orders
Send messengers to negotiate peace with the remaining kings
questions.correctAnswer: Pursue their enemies and do not stop until they are defeated
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:19 instructs the army not to stay but to pursue the enemies, smite the hindmost, and prevent them from entering their cities because the LORD had delivered them into Israel's hands.

questions.question: What happened after Joshua and the Israelites finished slaying their enemies?
options: The remaining enemies entered fenced cities
questions.correctAnswer: The remaining enemies entered fenced cities
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:20 explains that after the great slaughter, the rest of the enemy survivors fled into fortified cities, showing how the pursuit forced remaining foes to retreat.

questions.question: What was the condition of the Israelite camp after the pursuit and battles?
options: The camp was peaceful with no one speaking against Israel
The camp was divided and fearful
The camp was preparing for a counterattack
questions.correctAnswer: The camp was peaceful with no one speaking against Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:21 states that all the people returned in peace and that none spoke against the children of Israel, indicating unity and confidence after God's deliverance.

questions.question: When Joshua had the five kings brought out of the cave, what did he command the commanders to do?
options: Put their feet upon the necks of the kings
Release them as a sign of mercy
Bind them and send them to Gilgal
Offer them a chance to surrender
questions.correctAnswer: Put their feet upon the necks of the kings
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:24 records Joshua commanding the captains of the men of war to come near and put their feet upon the necks of the kings as a symbol of total victory and authority.

questions.question: What encouragement did Joshua give to the Israelite captains before executing the kings?
options: Fear not, be strong and courageous because the LORD will fight for you
Be cautious and wait for the LORD’s sign
Show mercy to the kings for they are defeated
Prepare for a long battle ahead
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not, be strong and courageous because the LORD will fight for you
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:25 contains Joshua’s exhortation to the captains not to fear or be dismayed but to be strong and courageous, trusting that the LORD will do to their enemies as promised.

questions.question: How were the five kings executed after being brought out of the cave?
options: They were smitten, slain, and hanged on five trees until evening
They were imprisoned until the war ended
They were released after pledging allegiance
They were put under house arrest
questions.correctAnswer: They were smitten, slain, and hanged on five trees until evening
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:26 describes how Joshua smote and slew the kings and then hanged them on five trees until the evening, demonstrating total defeat and public humiliation.

questions.question: What did Joshua command to be done with the kings' bodies at sunset?
options: Take them down from the trees and cast them into the cave, sealing it with stones
Leave them hanging overnight as a warning
Bury them near the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: Take them down from the trees and cast them into the cave, sealing it with stones
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:27 explains that at sunset, Joshua ordered the kings to be taken down and cast back into the cave where they had hidden, and the cave's mouth was sealed with great stones, signifying finality.

questions.question: What was the fate of the city of Makkedah on that day?
options: It was taken and utterly destroyed with none remaining
It was besieged but not captured
It became a part of Israel without violence
questions.correctAnswer: It was taken and utterly destroyed with none remaining
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:28 reports that Joshua took Makkedah and utterly destroyed it with the sword, leaving no survivors, as he had done with Jericho’s king and city.

questions.question: Which city did Joshua attack immediately after Makkedah?
questions.correctAnswer: Libnah
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:29 specifies that after taking Makkedah, Joshua and all Israel went to Libnah and fought against it, continuing their conquest.

questions.question: How does the conquest of Libnah illustrate God's faithfulness according to the passage?
options: The LORD delivered Libnah and its king into Israel’s hand, showing divine support
Libnah defeated Israel, showing human weakness
The conquest was uncertain and required long siege
Libnah was spared due to Israel’s mercy
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD delivered Libnah and its king into Israel’s hand, showing divine support
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:30 emphasizes that the LORD delivered Libnah and its king into Israel's hands, enabling a swift victory and demonstrating God's active role in Israel's battles.

questions.question: What does Joshua 10:19 teach about obedience and trust in God's promises during battle?
options: Pursuing enemies without delay leads to victory because God delivers them into your hand
Waiting and hesitating is wise to avoid casualties
Negotiations with enemies should always be attempted first
Retreating to defend cities is better than pursuing enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Pursuing enemies without delay leads to victory because God delivers them into your hand
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:19 instructs not to stay but to pursue enemies immediately, trusting that the LORD has delivered them into Israel's hand, illustrating the importance of obedience and faith in God's promises.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua commanded his men to show mercy to the five kings after capturing them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:26 shows that Joshua smote, slew, and hanged the kings, indicating no mercy was shown to them.

questions.question: True or False: The great stones placed on the cave’s mouth after the kings were cast in remained until that day.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:27 states that the stones laid on the cave's mouth remained until that very day, indicating a lasting memorial of the event.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 10.

questions.question: Which city did Joshua and all Israel encamp against after passing from Libnah?
questions.correctAnswer: Lachish
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:31 states that Joshua passed from Libnah to Lachish and encamped against it.

questions.question: How long did it take for Israel to take Lachish after the LORD delivered it into their hand?
questions.correctAnswer: Two days
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:32 records that Israel took Lachish on the second day after the LORD delivered it to them.

questions.question: Who came to help Lachish and was subsequently defeated by Joshua?
questions.correctAnswer: Horam king of Gezer
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:33 identifies Horam king of Gezer as coming to aid Lachish and being defeated by Joshua.

questions.question: Which city did Joshua and Israel fight against immediately after Lachish?
questions.correctAnswer: Eglon
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:34 says Joshua passed from Lachish to Eglon and fought against it.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua utterly destroyed all the souls in Eglon on the same day they took it.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:35 confirms Joshua and Israel smote and utterly destroyed all the souls in Eglon on that day.

questions.question: After Eglon, which city did Joshua capture next?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebron
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:36 indicates Joshua went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

questions.question: What was the fate of Hebron and its king according to Joshua 10:37?
options: They were left with some survivors
They were utterly destroyed with none remaining
questions.correctAnswer: They were utterly destroyed with none remaining
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:37 states that Hebron, its king, and all the souls therein were utterly destroyed with none left remaining.

questions.question: Which city did Joshua fight against after returning to Debir?
questions.correctAnswer: Debir
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:38 and 10:39 show Joshua returned to Debir and fought against it, taking it and utterly destroying all souls therein.

questions.question: How does Joshua 10:40 describe the extent of Joshua’s conquest in terms of geographical areas?
options: The country of the hills, south, vale, and springs and all their kings
questions.correctAnswer: The country of the hills, south, vale, and springs and all their kings
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:40 details Joshua smote all the country of the hills, south, vale, springs and all their kings, utterly destroying all.

questions.question: From which place to which place did Joshua smite the enemies according to Joshua 10:41?
questions.correctAnswer: Kadeshbarnea to Gaza
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:41 states Joshua smote them from Kadeshbarnea even unto Gaza and all the country of Goshen unto Gibeon.

questions.question: What reason does Joshua 10:42 give for Joshua taking all these kings and their lands at one time?
options: Because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:42 explains Joshua took all these kings and their lands at one time because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua and all Israel returned to the camp at Gilgal after the conquests described in Joshua 10.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:43 states Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal after completing the conquests.

questions.question: Which earlier book of the Bible is referenced as containing the account of the sun standing still in Joshua 10:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Book of Jasher
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:13 specifically mentions that the event of the sun standing still is written in the Book of Jasher.

questions.question: In Joshua 10:12-14, what literary device is prominently used when Joshua commands the sun and moon to stand still?
questions.correctAnswer: Personification
questions.explanation: The sun and moon are spoken to as if they can obey commands, which is personification (Joshua 10:12-14).

questions.question: Which Hebrew word meaning 'utterly destroyed' or 'devoted to destruction' is reflected in Joshua’s actions against the cities and kings in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Cherem
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Cherem' means devoted to destruction, which is reflected in Joshua utterly destroying cities and kings (Joshua 10:28-39).

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD's command to Joshua, 'Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:8 shows God's omnipotence as He assures Joshua of victory by delivering their enemies into his hand, demonstrating God's all-powerful ability to control outcomes in battle.

questions.question: According to Joshua 10:11, what does the LORD's act of casting down great stones from heaven upon the Amorites primarily reveal about His nature?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in judgment
questions.explanation: The LORD's hailstones in Joshua 10:11 serve as an act of divine judgment against the Amorites, reflecting God's justice in punishing sin and opposition to His people.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Joshua's prayer for the sun and moon to stand still in Joshua 10:12-13?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over creation
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:12-13 reveals God's sovereignty over the natural order, as the heavenly bodies obey His command, emphasizing His control over time and cosmic events.

questions.question: How does Joshua 10:14 uniquely demonstrate God’s responsiveness to human prayer in the Old Testament?
options: It states there was no other day like it when the LORD hearkened to a man's voice
It shows God ignoring human requests
It records God’s silence in times of battle
It emphasizes human effort over divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: It states there was no other day like it when the LORD hearkened to a man's voice
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:14 highlights that the LORD uniquely responded to Joshua’s prayer by halting the sun and moon, an extraordinary divine intervention illustrating God's hearance of human petitions.

questions.question: What does the hiding and subsequent capture of the five Amorite kings in a cave (Joshua 10:16-23) symbolize about the futility of human opposition against God’s purposes?
options: Human rebellion against God is ultimately powerless
Human kings can defeat God’s people
Victory depends solely on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: Human rebellion against God is ultimately powerless
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:16-23 demonstrates that despite their attempt to hide, the kings were discovered and captured, symbolizing that opposition to God's will cannot ultimately succeed.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is emphasized by Joshua commanding the captains to put their feet on the necks of the kings (Joshua 10:24-25)?
options: Christ’s ultimate victory over enemies typified
The sovereignty of human authority over God
The futility of trusting in God
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s ultimate victory over enemies typified
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:24-25 typologically foreshadows Christ's victory over all enemies, as placing feet on necks signifies complete subjugation, reflecting the Messiah’s triumph in the New Testament (e.g., Romans 16:20).

questions.question: How does the repeated destruction of cities and kings throughout Joshua 10:28-39 reinforce the biblical doctrine of holiness and judgment?
options: God’s judgment purges sin to sanctify His people
God tolerates sin in the land
Victory is based on political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment purges sin to sanctify His people
questions.explanation: The thorough destruction in Joshua 10:28-39 illustrates God’s holiness requiring judgment against sin to sanctify the land and His covenant people, consistent with Old Testament holiness codes.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative connection is made by Joshua’s conquest from Kadeshbarnea to Gaza and Goshen as recorded in Joshua 10:41-42?
options: The fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to Israel
The establishment of Israel as a kingdom under David
The beginning of the Babylonian exile
The building of the Temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:41-42 connects to the redemptive promise God made to the patriarchs to give the Promised Land to Israel, marking a key historical fulfillment in the biblical narrative.

questions.question: What synthesis theological insight emerges when comparing Joshua 10:5 (the alliance of five kings) and Joshua 10:40 (the complete destruction of their forces)?
options: God’s power triumphs over human coalition against His covenant people
Human alliances are invincible against Israel
God’s judgment is limited to individuals, not groups
Wars depend solely on strategy, not divine help
questions.correctAnswer: God’s power triumphs over human coalition against His covenant people
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:5 and 10:40 together show that despite the united effort of five kings, God's power ensured Israel’s complete victory, affirming divine sovereignty over human plans.

questions.question: How does Joshua 10:26-27 illustrate the seriousness of sin and the finality of divine judgment in the Old Testament context?
options: The kings were executed and their bodies were publicly displayed then hidden away, symbolizing total defeat
The kings were forgiven and released
The kings were made Israelite allies
The kings were given land to rule
questions.correctAnswer: The kings were executed and their bodies were publicly displayed then hidden away, symbolizing total defeat
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:26-27 depicts execution and public display of judgment on the kings, then concealment in a cave sealed with stones, emphasizing the absolute and irrevocable nature of divine condemnation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that miraculous events like the sun standing still in Joshua 10:12-13 are mythological and not historical. What does Joshua 10:12-14 actually teach about God's intervention in history?
options: God can and does intervene supernaturally in history to fulfill His purposes
God is distant and uninvolved in human affairs
Natural events have no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: God can and does intervene supernaturally in history to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:12-14 records a real divine intervention where God halted celestial bodies to aid Israel, affirming God's active role in history, countering sceptical claims of myth.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God’s faithfulness is showcased by the repeated phrase 'as he had done to the king of Jericho' in Joshua 10:1, 28, 30, 32, 35, 37, 39?
options: God consistently fulfills His promises to defend and deliver His people
God abandons His people in battles
questions.correctAnswer: God consistently fulfills His promises to defend and deliver His people
questions.explanation: The repeated formula in Joshua 10 stresses God's faithfulness and consistency in delivering Israel's enemies to defeat, affirming His trustworthy character.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth is revealed by Joshua 10:6-7 and Joshua 10:20-21 concerning God's provision and the role of human responsibility in salvation history?
options: God provides deliverance but requires active human obedience and pursuit
Human effort alone secures salvation without God
God does everything without human involvement
Salvation is based on military might alone
questions.correctAnswer: God provides deliverance but requires active human obedience and pursuit
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:6-7 shows Israel calling for help and Joshua responding obediently; 10:20-21 shows victory after pursuit, teaching that divine deliverance operates through human obedience.

questions.question: How does the conquest narrative in Joshua 10:28-39 reflect the holiness of God and His requirement for separation from sin within His covenant people?
options: God commands total destruction to prevent contamination by sin
God tolerates sin in the land for convenience
God encourages blending with enemy nations
God’s holiness is unrelated to warfare
questions.correctAnswer: God commands total destruction to prevent contamination by sin
questions.explanation: The complete destruction of cities and kings in Joshua 10:28-39 demonstrates God’s holiness demanding separation from sin to maintain covenant purity.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by Joshua 10:42 where it says the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness and providential care
questions.explanation: Joshua 10:42 illustrates God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His promises and providentially fighting for His people, ensuring their victory.
